title: A Step-Level Reliability Gateway for Agentic Clinical Decision Support: Architecture and Edge Deployment
content: Large language model (LLM) agents now retrieve patient records, call risk models and draft alerts in clinical workflows, yet their safety checks usually inspect only the final output. We present a reliability gateway that checks each action a clinical agent proposes, before it runs, and allows it, defers it to a clinician or blocks it. The decision fuses five run-time signals: calibration among similar patients, subgroup calibration gaps, group-conditional conformal sets, drift state and alert timing, plus a check that alerts quote tool outputs correctly. We generated agent trajectories with a local 7-billion-parameter model on emergency department (MIMIC-IV-ED) and intensive care (eICU-CRD) cohorts, injected six fault types at known steps, froze thresholds on a tuning split and replayed held-out trajectories. In the emergency setting, the gateway stopped 62% of faulty trajectories at the fault step, against 31% for an output-only check, with false intervention on 7.0% of clean trajectories. On held-out intensive care hospitals, its drift signal deferred every request. On a Raspberry Pi 5 the 99th-percentile latency per gated action was 25.8 ms, almost all of it from the nearest-neighbour signal, which added no measurable detection in the emergency setting. Step-level gating is feasible on embedded hardware; which signals are worth their cost depends on the deployment.
